chapter: South America and back in New York
title: Lending Louis Metcalf to Duke Ellington
summary: When Edith Wilson asks, Wooding lends trumpeter Louis Metcalf to cover Ellington's show at the Cotton Club, and says Duke had a sound while his band was merely good.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, when Duke came into the Cotton Louis Metcalf Club, they would allow that. So I loaned Duke Dewey Maycare Louis Metcalf I loaned him Dewey Maycare because they could not play the show at the time. They were a young band and they didn't know what it was all about. Edith Wilson was working with us in vaudeville. And she asked me, what could I do for Duke, could I help him out with anybody. Because they needed a good strong trumpet player. Because Bubba wasn't a good musician as far as reading was concerned. In fact, he had quite a few men in the band that couldn't read at that time. There was four or five of them that wasn't good readers at all. See, and they couldn't cut the show, so she said to me, "Could you loan Duke a man that would help him to put his show over?" I loaned him, so I said, the better man that he should have was Louis Metcalf. He was very good at that time. In fact, he was on a par with any of them at that time. So, I went to the theater manager and I said, "Look." And he said, "alright for the last show, when Miss Wilson goes in to do her doubling at the Cotton Club, could one of the men go out. We can play very well without him." So he said, "Well, I'll see how it comes this show. If this show works out, tomorrow, well I think for my audience, you can, he can get off, excused for the show." And he didn't cut nothing off the salary, either. So, anyhow, everything worked all right, so Louis Met-
-calf went to the Cotton Club and was a lifesaver for Duke Ellington at the time.

But, Chris just asked me, do I think we would have the same success, and I told him I didn't think so. Because if we had gone, or say any other band had gone up there, we'd have played maybe two months, and that would be the end of it. But, because we were just a good band, but an ordinary band. Duke had a sound.
